R834.note: password_verify() correctly replaces loose `==`, but by this point $user is always truthy (function already returned earlier if !$user), so the DUMMY_HASH/user-not-found branch is dead code; more importantly the fix requires the stored password column to already hold a hash, which the original plaintext-comparison strongly implies it does not - write-up discloses this migration prerequisite openly, so a silent break becomes a disclosed one.

R835.note: Adds control-character escaping plus SLF4J {} placeholders on both paths; contract preserved (ERROR+exception+401, INFO+200) and the extra success-path fix is justified and stated.

R836.note: Switching to SLF4J {} placeholders alone does not strip or escape \r/\n - the argument's raw toString() is written verbatim, so a crafted username still forges log lines; the vector is not actually closed (contrast with sibling write-up R835 on the same case, which adds explicit control-character escaping). No other behavior changed.

R837.note: Removing the tainted envp array entirely stops untrusted data reaching exec(); no legitimate functionality depended on that env array (it was never read back).

R838.note: sqlite3 `?` placeholder with bound tuple correctly parameterizes; exact-match search behavior preserved, matches contract.

R839.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID-based filename closes both the dangerous-type and path-traversal angles; response shape (stored name, byte count, 400 on empty) preserved; narrowing to safe extensions is the intended CWE-434 remediation, not incidental scope creep.

R840.note: keyFunc method-type assertion plus jwt.WithValidMethods (real golang-jwt/v5 API) closes the alg-confusion vector without touching the success path for legitimate HS256 tokens; needed fmt import is disclosed.

R841.note: Does not compile: concatenating two `$"..."` interpolated strings with `+` produces a plain `string`, not `FormattableString`, so passing the result to ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync fails with CS1503 (verified by compiling the exact snippet with dotnet build: 'cannot convert from string to System.FormattableString'). Undisclosed - breaks the endpoint entirely.

R842.note: Server-owned ALLOWED_TABLES map used as a key rather than validating raw input, matching the prescribed pattern; default ledger_entries and bound accountId/status preserved per contract.

R843.note: Adding getSessionIdentifier correctly binds tokens to the session and closes the reported gap, but the fix rewrites the csrf-csrf config inline in accountRoutes.js (leaving the flagged csrfProtection.js untouched/orphaned) and adds an undisclosed hardcoded fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') when CSRF_SECRET is unset - a new, silent weakness that lets an attacker forge valid tokens with a known secret in that misconfiguration case, worse than the original's fail-with-undefined-secret behavior.

R844.note: self.get_object() applies both get_queryset() scoping and has_object_permission, producing the required indistinguishable-404 behavior for staff/owner/other exactly per contract.

R845.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() before dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the standard, appropriate closure; legitimate formatted descriptions still render. (Could not verify the cited CVE-2026-41238/3.4.0 claim without web access; does not affect the code fix itself.)

R846.note: random_bytes/random_int correctly replace the seeded mt_rand CSPRNG weakness, but the primary recommended token (64-char hex) is a drastic format change from the original short numeric code the mail text calls 'this code' (implying manual entry) - disclosed via an explicit numeric alternative, so the breaking-format risk is stated rather than silent.

R847.note: disallow-doctype-decl plus external-entity/DTD disabling is the standard, complete XXE closure; legitimate orderXml (no DOCTYPE) is unaffected, each setFeature/setAttribute call is defensively wrapped.

R848.note: Right general strategy (verify ownership before delete) but neither option fits the given stub files as-is: Option 1 calls repository.findById()/doc.getOwnerId() on types that don't exist anywhere in the case and isn't flagged as an addition (unlike Option 2, which explicitly redefines repository/service); Option 1's @PreAuthorize denial also yields a default 403, which the write-up's own explanation admits differs from Option 2's 404, conflicting with the contract's 'should not reveal more than the existing not-found path' for one of the two presented fixes.

R849.note: ValidAlgorithms whitelist is the correct, minimal fix for algorithm-confusion in TokenValidationParameters; no other behavior touched.

R850.note: Canonical-path resolution plus prefix check (with separator) correctly closes traversal regardless of the double-decode or absolute-path quirks in File(parent,child); legitimate in-directory filenames still resolve and serve normally.
